summary: Full backend + frontend regression after the FastAPI + MongoDB migration. Wrote /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with 23 pytest cases across health, seller/customer/rider auth, multi-seller catalog, per-seller order split, rider onboarding, full delivery loop with server-owned OTP, and rider live-location endpoint — 23/23 PASSED. Frontend E2E via Playwright verified: multi-seller shop filter (data-testid shop-filter with pills for both sellers), cross-seller product cards showing seller name, cloud-sync JWT session persistence across page reload, Rider Onboarding UI (Delivery Riders tab -> Add Rider -> credentials shown once as RIDER-XXXX + rider-card rendered), new-rider login via delivery portal, and Live Rider Map on customer OrderTracker (data-testid live-rider-map with Google Maps iframe + LIVE badge, and customer-delivery-otp exactly matching the server-generated OTP). Regression: location picker still opens correctly for logged-in customers (title 'Delivery Distance & Address' visible).

ui_bugs.issue: Whole app crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading maxQtyKm5)' if ANY product in /api/products lacks a distanceRules object. The seller UI's ProductManagerModal defaults distanceRules on save, but the backend POST /api/products accepts arbitrary JSON — so a product created by any client (or a partial migration) that omits distanceRules bricks the entire customer catalog with a white screen. Please guard with optional chaining + safe fallback (e.g. `product.distanceRules?.maxQtyKm5 ?? Infinity`) OR enforce/normalize distanceRules on the backend in POST /api/products before persistence.

OrderTracker crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading fullName)' when an order lacks a top-level `address` object (line 524 selectedOrder.address.fullName, and lines 525/527 for streetAddress/city/pincode/phone). App.tsx's handlePlaceOrder always sets `address` correctly so real UI flows are fine, but any order created out-of-band (integration, historical, or partial data) crashes the entire tracker page. Recommend defensive access: `selectedOrder.address?.fullName` with fallback text, or backend validation that requires the address block on POST /api/orders.
Still using cdn.tailwindcss.com — production warning printed on every load. Move to the PostCSS build already configured.

action_items: Add optional-chaining guards for product.distanceRules access in services/storage.ts and ProductCatalog.tsx (or normalize distanceRules server-side in POST /api/products).
Add optional-chaining guards in OrderTracker.tsx around selectedOrder.address.* (or require address in POST /api/orders schema).
Move Tailwind off cdn.tailwindcss.com to the PostCSS/CLI build.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py POST /api/products & POST /api/orders accept `body: dict` with no Pydantic validation, so malformed products/orders can silently corrupt the DB and crash the frontend. Introduce Pydantic models (ProductCreate, OrderCreate) with required fields (distanceRules, address).
App.tsx is >660 lines and services/storage.ts still ships helpers that assume required nested fields — split by role view + centralize schema-defensive selectors.
OrderTracker & ProductCatalog have no error boundary; a single missing nested field white-screens the whole customer app.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is solid — 23/23 pass and all endpoints (auth for 3 roles, multi-seller product filtering, per-seller order enforcement in GET /api/orders, rider onboarding CRUD, rider location, full seller->rider order state loop) behave correctly. The remaining risk is on the frontend defensive-coding side: any product row missing distanceRules whitescreens the catalog, and any order missing top-level `address` whitescreens the tracker. These are triggered by malformed/backfilled/API-created data, not by the normal UI flow. Fix by adding optional-chaining + fallbacks (fastest) and/or by tightening backend Pydantic validation on POST /api/products and POST /api/orders. After that fix, re-run the same Playwright multi-seller + tracker flow (a second seller registered via UI with a product, plus a customer order advanced to Out for Delivery with a rider location) to confirm the app survives partial data. Live-rider-map (Google Maps iframe embed) and customer-delivery-otp are confirmed to render correctly when data is well-formed.
rca_of_the_issue: storage.ts and OrderTracker.tsx directly dereference nested product.distanceRules.* and selectedOrder.address.* without null-guards. Because server.py accepts arbitrary JSON for POST /api/products and POST /api/orders (body: dict, no Pydantic model), any client (including future integrations, imports, or these tests) can insert documents that satisfy MongoDB but violate the frontend's implicit shape contract, causing a full-tree React crash (no error boundary). The safe fixes are (a) frontend optional-chaining/defaults, and (b) backend schema validation with Pydantic ProductCreate/OrderCreate.
